title: Exclusive-allocation repair persistence audit
question: Is EXCLUSIVE_ALLOCATION_BRANCH_MISSING persistence primarily caused by an insufficient repair card, an overly broad error family, or another architectural effect?
hypothesis: The family conflates absent nodes, invalid nodes, and missing links, while overlapping topology cards create competing repair instructions.

change_under_test.description: Classify historical firings by raw candidate structure and correlate them with co-firing invariants and next-attempt persistence.

control.description: Existing unsplit invariant and restore-exclusive-allocation-branch repair card.

intentionally_not_compared: prospective repair success after splitting the family
validator detection precision against manually labeled gold
interpretation: The evidence does not support treating persistence as a single weak-card problem. The invariant combines at least absent-branch, absent-intermediate, invalid-or-unrecognized-node, and missing-link situations. It also duplicates MISSING_PROCESS_INTERMEDIATE in most affected attempts. Because completeness errors are emitted alongside prerequisite source/type errors, repair cards can target a downstream symptom before the proposed node is structurally admissible.

do_not_prioritize: making the existing monolithic card longer
adding more full-source context to every allocation repair
decision.next_test: Split the diagnostic into allocation anchor missing, nonreceipt node absent, nonreceipt node invalid, nonreceipt link missing, and stipulated outcome missing; route only the earliest actionable prerequisite and test each card on frozen positive/negative candidates.

limitations: Historical diagnostics span multiple code versions and repeated attempts.
Raw rejected candidates are not always identical to the normalized typed model at the point of failure.
A lexical audit can identify nonreceipt-like material but cannot by itself prove that the node was admissible.
Prospective split-card performance has not yet been measured.
